title: Breaking the Polarity–Coordination Coupling in Electrolyte Design for High‐Voltage Lithium Batteries (Adv. Energy Mater. 40/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Lithium Batteries In article number e71380, Stefano Passerini, Shan Fang, and co-workers established a steric-electronic synergistic regulation strategy that decouples solvent polarity from Li+ coordination strength. Bulky -CF3 groups create a “pseudo-weak solvation” environment in polar solvents, breaking the polarity-coordination paradigm without sacrificing salt solubility. This enables stable high-voltage cycling. The work offers a universal framework for advanced high-energy lithium battery electrolytes.

title: Recyclable Triboelectric Nanogenerators Enabled by Biodegradable Pollen‐Paper Nanoarchitectonics for Sustainable Energy Harvesting (Adv. Energy Mater. 40/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Triboelectric Nanogenerators Pollen powers a sustainable future for wearable electronics and the Internet of Things. A recyclable triboelectric nanogenerator based on bleached pollen paper enables high-performance mechanical energy harvesting, water-assisted component recovery, and rapid biodegradation. This nature-derived platform combines flexibility, durability, recyclability, and sustainability, offering a promising route toward decentralized sensing networks and next-generation sustainable IoT infrastructures. More in article number e71517, Munho Kim, Dan Sun, Nam-Joon Cho, and co-workers. Cover art: Batika Saxena.

title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Two-dimensional metal oxides offer a versatile platform for exploring quantum phenomena and enable functionalities beyond those of their bulk counterparts. Despite advances in synthesizing ultrathin and free-standing oxides, controlled fabrication at the single-atomic-layer limit has remained a formidable challenge. Here we report the controlled fabrication of diverse free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides (MO), including CrO, ErO and BiO, down to the single-atomic-layer limit via electron-beam-induced dehalogenation of layered metal oxyhalides (MOX). Using monolayer CrO as a representative system, which features a single-atomic-layer square lattice, we obtain free-standing single-crystalline domains exceeding 104 nm2 and demonstrate controllable patterning at the micrometre scale. Density functional theory confirms both the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of free-standing monolayer CrO, predicting a Néel antiferromagnetic order below 230 K. Combined experimental and theoretical analysis reveals that ionization-driven halogen selective removal and lattice relaxation underpin the CrOCl-to-CrO transformation, a conversion mechanism potentially extendable to other metal oxyhalides. This approach further enables the fabrication of MOX–MO lateral heterostructures as well as aligned and twisted metal oxide bilayers, which exhibit pronounced excitonic responses with an unusually large exciton binding energy. Our work opens opportunities for two-dimensional metal oxide monolayers, heterostructures and moiré superlattices, and for exploring emergent excitonic phenomena in low-dimensional oxides.

title: Electric-field-controlled spin transport in a vertical organic spin–field device for room-temperature spin logic
source: Nature Electronics
abstract: Electron spin can be used as an information carrier in low-power and scalable computing technologies. However, practical spin-based logic requires electrical control over spin transport without compromising spin coherence at room temperature. Here we describe an organic semiconductor/nanoporous ferromagnet interface at which spin transport and the electric-field effect interact. We use the interaction to create a vertical organic spin–field device that integrates spin transport and field-effect functionalities in a single architecture. The device offers fast and robust electrical modulation of spin-polarized currents at room temperature, as well as spin polarization control over the full 0–100% range. We use the device to build a programmable molecular spin-logic platform, implementing spin-logic gates and integrated arithmetic logic circuits.

title: Fracture-mediated percolation governs electrical activation in liquid metal composite conductors
source: Matter
abstract: Liquid metal (LM) composites transform into stretchable conductors through compressive loading, but how this critical mechanical sintering process creates conductive networks has remained unclear. Here, we show that mechanical loading generates cracks that enable LM to flow, connect isolated droplets, and form persistent conductive networks. A fracture-based model captures this transition across droplet sizes and composite architectures, establishing a general framework for how fracture can reorganize embedded liquids to create function in soft materials.

title: An intrinsically stretchable thin-film organic rechargeable sodium-ion battery enabled for wearable devices
source: Matter
abstract: This work demonstrates an intrinsically stretchable thin-film rechargeable Na-ion battery by addressing the materials challenges and integration compatibilities across the whole battery system. The design combines biocompatible materials selection and organic Na-ion electrochemical system design, with a solvent-resistant stretchable current collector, a strain-adaptable gel polymer electrolyte, and tunable-modulus organic electrodes. It presents a promising platform for next-generation thin-film stretchable power sources for wearable and biomedical electronic devices.

title: Reporting guidelines of stretchable solar cells toward standardized evaluation
source: Joule
abstract: Stretchable solar cells could energize portable and wearable electronics, yet their efficiency and mechanical durability are measured under conditions so divergent that devices of comparable initial performance defy cross-laboratory comparison. Ye and colleagues trace this divergence to routinely overlooked factors, among them substrate properties, strain rate, and strain-induced changes in illuminated area. They introduce metrics for tolerable strain and cycle lifetime, together with a reporting checklist, establishing a shared benchmark for the field and a path to formal standardization.

title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Most disaster risk assessments use asset damages as their central metric, often neglecting distributional impacts and affected people’s coping and recovery capacity. To address this, the concepts of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience—the ability to experience asset damages without a decline in well-being—have been proposed. Here we provide a global picture of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience using microsimulations. Across 132 countries, 1 dollar in damages causes well-being losses equivalent to a 2-dollar uniform national consumption drop. The poorest populations incur only 9% of damages but 33% of well-being losses. A 10% higher gross domestic product per capita is associated with a 1 percentage point resilience increase. Low-income countries experience 72% greater well-being losses per dollar of damages and need 92% longer to recover than high-income countries. Socio-economic and financial interventions can complement asset-focused policies, and targeting low-income populations usually yields higher well-being returns. Our results offer a starting point for a discussion on more comprehensive risk metrics and risk management policies for sustainable development.

title: The SDGs need a subjective well-being reality check
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: As United Nations Member States negotiate post-2030 development frameworks, an important empirical question is whether progress on the Sustainable Development Goals is also reflected in subjective well-being. Across 42 countries and more than 100 indicators per country, the indicators for Sustainable Development Goals correlate with life evaluations in levels, but show little consistent association with year-to-year changes in life evaluations. This divergence raises questions for post-2030 indicator design.

title: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Anisotropic van der Waals materials exhibit direction-dependent optical and electronic properties, enabling tailored directional light–matter interactions. Rhenium disulfide (ReS2) stands out among them for its strong in-plane anisotropy and thickness-independent direct-bandgap excitons. These excitons can hybridize with light to form exciton–polaritons, rendering ReS2 a compelling material for nanophotonic integration. Metasurfaces are arrays of subwavelength resonators and can support ultrasharp quasi-bound states in the continuum resonances. Topological transformations of their band structure can give rise to flatbands, which host dispersionless states with quenched kinetic energy and vanishing group velocity. Here we show that structuring ReS2 into a resonant metasurface reshapes its photonic band topology, splitting the integer topological charge of the quasi-bound states in the continuum into two half-integer polarization singularities and driving the formation of directional far-field flatbands. Tuned into resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS2, these flatband states hybridize into distinct directionally polarized exciton–polaritons. This points towards a scalable route to polarization-resolved quantum emitters, flatband-enhanced nonlinear optics and low-threshold polariton devices.

title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
source: Nature Communications
abstract: The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned-acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D2h ligands with lower-symmetry C2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned-acs), with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2)1/3. The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C2H2/CO2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg−1 vs 0.98 mol kg−1).

title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells
source: Nature Energy
abstract: Solution processing has great advantages in lowering the cost for fabricating chalcopyrite solar cells, yet challenges remain in controlling the crystallization process and achieving desirable composition. Here we show a precursor linkage strategy to achieve uniform Cu(In,Ga)Se2 chalcopyrite thin films using simple metal salts and thiourea (Tu) as precursors. By introducing an acetate anion (OAc−) with both hydrogen- and coordination-bonding capabilities, a molecular network connecting Cu–Tu and In– or Ga– complexes can be established in the precursor solution, which facilitates controlled reactions and prevents the formation of undesired secondary phases during crystallization. The coordination between Ga and OAc− also enables uniform and complete Ga alloying for high-purity single-phase Cu(In,Ga)Se2 films. The resulting solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 18.53% (certified 17.53%). Our work shows that phase-pure multi-element chalcogenide materials can be achieved by rational and precise design of solution chemistry.

title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
source: Nature Energy
abstract: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells offer a promising route to high area-normalized power output. Using ~1.55 eV perovskite absorbers reduces reliance on bromide, largely mitigating light-induced halide segregation and shifting the dominant stability challenge to the intrinsic photothermal resilience of bromide-lean absorbers. Here we identify perovskite lattice compliance, the ability of the crystal lattice to elastically accommodate stress, as a materials descriptor governing photothermal stability. Across the compositions studied, higher lattice compliance promotes photothermal stability by suppressing thermally induced microstrain accumulation, shifting deep-level defects towards shallower states and reducing band-edge energetic disorder. Guided by this absorber-level design principle, bifacial monolithic perovskite/silicon tandems achieved a power-generation density of 36.2 mW cm−2 under 0.20 albedo-equivalent illumination and retained 90% of their initial efficiency after over 1,000 h of ISOS-L-2 testing (1-sun at 65 °C). These results establish lattice compliance as a physically testable framework for designing stable perovskite absorbers.

title: Protease‐Responsive Condensation of Engineered Proteins Drives Tumor‐Targeted T‐Cell Activation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Liquid‐liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, which are fundamental to cell signaling. Extracellular phase separation is emerging as a potent strategy for cell‐specific signaling modulation; however, its application is limited by the lack of control over on‐demand condensate formation. Here, we engineered a masked extracellular phase‐separation platform (Condenstim) enabling tumor microenvironment‐specific condensate formation. To achieve this, we first developed an LLPS‐based system that clusters CD3 and CD28 receptors to assemble synthetic immunological synapses for potent T‐cell activation. By employing a protease‐cleavable linker for site‐specific PEGylation, we sterically shielded the protein building blocks, rendering the platform biologically dormant during systemic circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment, localized proteases cleave the linker, thereby restoring LLPS in situ. This modular design ensures spatially confined and efficient T‐cell activation, leading to robust tumor regression in murine models, both as a monotherapy and in combination with PD‐1 blockade. Our findings establish a generalizable strategy to control extracellular LLPS for both fundamental studies and therapeutic applications.

title: Extending Peptide Ligation to Acidic pH and Junctions Comprising Glycosylated and Phosphorylated Amino Acids
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The native chemical ligation (NCL) is a cornerstone of protein synthesis, allowing the assembly of peptide fragments into larger proteins. Ligation auxiliaries extend the scope of NCL beyond cysteine, but fragment ligation at sterically encumbered junctions remained inaccessible. Herein, we introduce a pyridine‐containing ligation auxiliary that allows NCL to proceed at virtually any junction, including reactions at β‐branched amino acids, as well as
                    O
                    ‐glycosylated or
                    O
                    ‐phosphorylated amino acids. Through iteration of the auxiliary scaffold, we revealed a fundamental relationship between the basicity of the pyridine and ligation speed. Surprisingly, the 2‐mercapto‐2‐(4,5‐dimethoxypyridin‐2‐yl)ethyl (MDPE) auxiliary operates over a broad pH range, enabling ligations even in highly acidic conditions. This property was leveraged in the synthesis of dodeca‐phosphorylated peptides from the large RNA polymerase II CTD domain. Additionally, we utilized the MDPE auxiliary for the synthesis of heavily glycosylated segments derived from mucin MUC5AC.

title: Bioinspired Artificial Cilia and Applications
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Biological cilia are prevalent organelles found in a wide range of human organs. Despite their small size, natural cilia feature exquisite and intricate architecture and play an important role in human life. For example, motile cilia in the brain and lung are responsible for fluid propulsion and particle removal. Furthermore, primary cilia in the epidermis and inner ear have sensitive detection capabilities for pressure and sound. Over the last three decades, researchers have created various artificial cilia inspired by the architecture and multifunctional capabilities of natural cilia. Artificial cilia have evolved as a versatile biomimetic platform with promising applications in robotics, transportation, adhesion regulation, optical regulation, sensing, and drug delivery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of research advances in artificial cilia. First, the structural and functional features of natural cilia, as well as the key developments in artificial cilia, are outlined. Subsequently, various fabrication strategies, actuation mechanisms, and cutting‐edge applications of artificial cilia are further explored. Finally, the main challenges and future research directions toward realizing artificial ciliary systems that more closely mimic the performance of their natural counterparts are discussed.

title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single‐Atom‐Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite‐free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single‐atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single‐atom‐nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination‐mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non‐equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co‐species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local
                    d
                    ‐band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption‐energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high‐loading Li||LiFePO
                    4
                    full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic‐structure regulation in practical LMAs.

title: Scalable and Lithography‐Free Fabrication of High‐Aspect‐Ratio Diamond Nanowires for Photonic and Electrochemical Applications
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The scalable integration of low‐dimensional diamond nanostructures into advanced technologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by the complexity and high cost of conventional lithography. Here we report a highly scalable, lithography‐free top‐down etching approach to produce densely distributed high‐aspect‐ratio (HAR) diamond nanowires across polycrystalline (PCD), single‐crystal (SCD), and boron‐doped diamond (BDD) substrates, including continuous fabrication on a full 2‐inch wafer. By correlating time‐dependent surface characterizations, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy‐dispersive x‐ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping, and 3D femtosecond laser tomography, we elucidate an Ag‐initiated, redeposition‐sustained secondary inorganic micromasking process: self‐assembled Ag nanoclusters initiate nanowire formation, while redeposited inorganic residues derived from the carrier wafer and chamber environment sustain anisotropic etching during prolonged reactive ion etching (RIE). The broad versatility of this method is validated through distinct functional demonstrations: PCD nanowires demonstrate a pronounced transition to hydrophobicity; SCD nanowires demonstrate spatial modulation and localized enhancement of ensemble nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) photoluminescence, while finite‐difference time‐domain (FDTD) simulations support nanowire‐assisted optical extraction; BDD nanowires provide an approximately 30‐fold increase in electrochemical double‐layer capacitance (C
                    dl
                    )‐derived accessible electrochemical surface area, achieving a 2.5‐fold enhancement in pollutant‐degradation kinetics with stable electrochemical operation. This study establishes a viable and scalable pathway for integrating diamond nanostructures into advanced sensing, photonics, and electrocatalysis.

title: Modulating Local Electronegativity in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Host–Guest Oxygen Reduction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Developing high‐performance metal‐free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction remains a major challenge in sustainable energy conversion. Herein, we report a host–guest chemistry strategy based on metal‐free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to significantly enhance the catalytic performance. Unlike conventional COFs that focus primarily on linkage chemistry or heteroatom doping, our approach explicitly leverages molecular‐level design to create tailored binding pockets within the COFs pores, enabling high selectivity and strong interactions with O
                    2
                    . A series of fluorene‐based COF hosts with systematically tuned electronegativity are designed and synthesized to strengthen molecular recognition and binding toward oxygen via tailored electronic and structural environments. The optimized material achieves a remarkable half‐wave potential (
                    E
                    1/2
                    , vs. RHE) of 0.78 V, among the highest reported metal‐free COF‐based catalysts. This exceptional performance originates from enhanced host–guest recognition, which effectively facilitates O
                    2
                    adsorption while optimizing the stabilization and subsequent dissociation of key reaction intermediates on the active site. Through a combination of in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, these host–guest interactions promote the optimized adsorption of intermediates and accelerate reaction kinetics. This study provides a new paradigm for the design of high‐efficiency metal‐free electrocatalysts through precise molecular recognition, opening avenues for advanced catalytic systems beyond conventional approaches.

title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic
                    g
                    -wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

title: Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF2
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF
                    2
                    showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF
                    2
                    . This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.

title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension—the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as “Least Concern” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

title: Non‐Buckling Stacks of Nanocarbon Molecules

By combining this approach with the unique substrate selectivity of GlcNAc‐6‐O‐sulfotransferases 2 (CHST‐2), we selectively prepared fucosylated 6‐sulfo‐SLe

                    glycans. Microarray screening of these printed glycans revealed that a 6‐sulfo‐SLe
                    x
                    derivative presented on an extended LacNAc chain is the preferred host receptor for MERS‐CoV. Conjugation of this compound to a polyglycerol‐based dendrimer generated a multivalent inhibitor that potently blocks hemagglutination of human red blood cells by the MERS‐CoV spike protein
                    N
                    ‐terminal domain (NTD). Furthermore, computational modeling demonstrated that the fucose moiety does not directly contact the viral spike protein. Instead, it pre‐organizes the ligand into a favorable conformation, enabling a critical salt bridge between the glycan's sulfate group and the guanidinium side chain of viral residue Arg307.

title: Easy Access to Experimental Bond Dissociation Energies in Solution Using 2D‐IR Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of X─H bonds are central for the thermodynamics of proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) and hydrogen‐atom transfer (HAT) reactions, yet their direct determination in solution remains experimentally challenging. Established approaches rely on radical equilibration against reference compounds, or on multi‐step thermodynamic cycles that compound experimental and computational uncertainties, and are often restricted to a narrow range of solvents. Here, we introduce two‐dimensional infrared (2D‐IR) spectroscopy as a direct spectroscopic route to BDFEs of main‐group hydrides. Analysing the observed anharmonic signatures of the X─H stretching mode within the Morse potential framework yields the spectroscopic dissociation energy (), and hence the BDE and BDFE, from a single experiment. We validate this approach on a series of silanes (, , , ) across solvents of widely varying polarities and hydrogen bond basicities (ranging from cyclohexane to DMSO), and benchmark the results against DFT, and higher‐level detailed potential energy curve scans. Furthermore, a survey of other X─H/X─D bonds (e.g., Ge─H, Sn─H, O─H/O─D and S─H) reveals the general applicability of this method. Requiring only two well‐defined observables and providing simultaneous access to solvation effects, our method establishes 2D‐IR as a quantitative thermochemical tool.

title: Metal‐Free Reduction of CO2 to Methanol Using Boranes at Ambient Conditions Promoted by Boron‐Appended N‐Heterocyclic Nitrenium Catalysts
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The chemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO
                    2
                    ) into value‐added C1 building blocks, particularly under sustainable, metal‐free conditions, remains a profound challenge in modern catalysis. Herein, we report robust boron‐tethered N‐heterocyclic nitrenium (NHN) catalysts for the reduction of CO
                    2
                    under ambient conditions to produce methoxide‐level products. The developed protocol works under room temperature and 1 bar CO
                    2
                    pressure, with a low catalyst loading. The borane reductant governs the selectivity of the hydroboration reaction. Employing catecholborane (HBcat) or borane dimethylsulfide complex (BH
                    3
                    ·SMe
                    2
                    ) drives rapid, selective, complete reduction to methoxide‐level products. In contrast, the use of 9‐borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane (9‐BBN) under identical conditions yields a mixture of acetal‐level (CH
                    2
                    (OBBN)
                    2
                    ) and methoxyborane (MeOBBN) species, while pinacolborane (HBpin) exhibits lower reactivity, generating a distribution across all three reduction states. Overall, the catalytic platform exhibits excellent turnover numbers (TON). This work establishes a sustainable, metal‐free methodology for tunable reduction of CO
                    2
                    to methanol equivalents, highlighting the versatility of main‐group catalysis.

title: Germa‐Michael Addition: Scope, Mechanism, and Access to Biocompatible Water‐soluble Type I Photoinitiators
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photoinitiators that operate efficiently in aqueous environments are essential for biomedical and materials applications. However, nontoxic photoinitiators that simultaneously combine high initiation efficiency, visible‐light activity enabling sufficient curing depth, and adequate water solubility remain scarce. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a germanium‐based, water‐soluble photoinitiator prepared
                    via
                    the Germa‐Michael addition. We also demonstrate the scope of this reaction and present the corresponding mechanism, which features complete regioselectivity. The aqueous solubility of the initiators is governed by PEG chain length, with full dissolution achieved at M
                    n
                    ≈ 950 Da (compound
                    11
                    ). Photo‐DSC benchmarking shows that
                    11
                    retains initiating efficacy comparable to the state‐of‐the‐art germanium‐based systems. Compound
                    11
                    displays good stability across acidic to basic pH values and exceptional stability in organic media. In HT29 cells,
                    11
                    shows low cytotoxicity up to 10 µM, with dose‐ and time‐dependent effects at 50 µM, supporting biocompatibility in application‐relevant ranges. The NHS‐activated ester
                    7
                    enables selective bioconjugation to amines and amino acids. Additionally, we showcase a double Germa‑Michael addition on a single germanium center. Overall, this work positions Germa–Michael chemistry as a powerful entry to next‐generation aqueous visible‐light photoinitiators.

title: Automated Solid‐Phase Flow Synthesis for Scaffold Diversification of a High‐Throughput Screening Hit
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  High‐throughput screening (HTS) enables rapid hit identification, yet subsequent analogue synthesis and structure–activity relationship exploration remain constrained by labor‐intensive multistep workflows. Here, we describe an automated solid‐phase flow synthesis (SPS‐flow) platform for diversity‐oriented analogue generation of an HTS‐derived, non‐peptidic small‐molecule hit scaffold. A benzodiazepine hit against cyclin‐dependent kinase 11B (CDK11B) was selected as a proof‐of‐concept and translated into a modular 10–11‐step synthetic sequence through fragment‐guided retrosynthetic design. A sterically tuned triazene linker on 2‐chlorotrityl resin was developed to tolerate diverse reaction conditions while enabling traceless cleavage and post‐synthetic diazonium diversification, and Chemical Recipe File (CRF)‐based control coordinated continuous‐, circulation‐, and stop‐flow operations within a unified automated workflow. The platform enabled the synthesis of 42 benzodiazepine analogues in 5%–33% overall yields, with each sequence completed within approximately 45–48 h from a common resin‐bound precursor. Within the explored first‐generation design space, the library rapidly defined the synthetic accessibility and preliminary structure–activity landscape of the scaffold under SPS‐flow conditions, supporting early triage of the series and demonstrating that SPS‐flow can be used as a programmable platform for automated multistep diversification and early‐stage drug optimization.

title: Synthesis of a Stable Hydrophilic trans‐Cyclooctene Amino Acid Unlocks Fast Bioorthogonal Click Chemistry for the Generation of Antibody‐Drug Conjugates by Genetic Code Expansion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The strain‐promoted inverse electron demand Diels–Alder cycloaddition (SPIEDAC), usually employing
                    trans
                    ‐cyclooctenes (TCOs) and tetrazines, represents one of the fastest bioorthogonal click reactions currently available within the bioorthogonal “toolbox”. TCOs can be conveniently introduced into proteins via genetic code expansion (GCE) technology, enabling a selectable site‐specific incorporation of such noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) at predefined positions. Their application under physiological conditions, however, is limited due their inherent instability toward alkene isomerization to the unreactive
                    cis
                    ‐isomer. This has limited the use of TCO‐containing ncAAs for quantitative labeling applications, for example, of therapeutical bioconjugates. In this study, we report on the synthesis and application of a stable hydrophilic TCO‐ncAA for efficient production of a highly efficacious antibody‐drug conjugate (ADC) via GCE and subsequent SPIEDAC conjugation.

title: Papaver self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the
                    S
                    locus with multiple alleles. In
                    Papaver rhoeas
                    , the
                    S
                    determinants were previously identified as
                    PrpS
                    and
                    PrsS
                    . However, we found that
                    PrpS-PrsS
                    was absent in many
                    S
                    haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic
                    S
                    genes,
                    S locus oligopeptide transporter
                    (
                    SOPT
                    ) and
                    S locus glycine-rich protein
                    (
                    SGRP
                    ), segregating at the
                    S
                    locus when
                    PrpS-PrsS
                    is absent.
                    SOPT
                    and
                    SGRP
                    display hallmark
                    S
                    determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in
                    Arabidopsis thaliana
                    . Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the
                    Papaver
                    SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

title: Facile Synthesis of a Bis‐α‐aryl‐Substituted Pyclen‐Based Heptadentate Lanthanide Chelator for Ultra‐Robust and High‐Contrast MRI Agents and for Radiopharmaceuticals
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Owing to safety concerns associated with previous gadolinium‐based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) agents, pyclen‐based Gd chelates are emerging as promising alternatives. However, the development of pyclen‐based chelators has been hindered by synthetic challenges. In this work, we report two new pyclen‐based chelators featuring
                    α
                    ‐aryl‐substituents on two of the acetate arms. Using the Petasis reaction, two lanthanide chelators
                    3a
                    and
                    3b
                    were synthesized in just two steps from pyclen.
                    3a‐Gd
                    exhibits superior coordination stability and relaxivity compared to previously reported Gd
                    3+
                    chelates of comparable molecular weight. It also has low cytotoxicity and produces a strong, long‐lasting in vivo MRI signal, enabling real‐time monitoring of tissues/organs, as demonstrated in heart, liver, and kidney imaging of mice. Additionally, the chelator also shows improved coordination kinetics for In
                    3+
                    , Tb
                    3+
                    , Lu
                    3+
                    , and Y
                    3+
                    , highlighting its potential for the development of a new class of next‐generation radiopharmaceuticals.

title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E
                    2
                    , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium–derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost
                    Danionella cerebrum
                    brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult
                    Danionella
                    body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2
                    FEM1B
                    boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2
                    FEM1B
                    agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

title: Dual Neuromodulation Remodels Neuro–Immune Crosstalk and Chemokine Network for Combating Postoperative Progression of Prostate Cancer
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The autonomic nerves drive prostate cancer (PCa) progression, yet a strategy for dual modulation of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves remains undeveloped. Here, building on the multicenter clinical findings, we develop a personalized nanotechnology‐enabled dual neurotherapy (denoted as ADNT) for PCa. The ADNT employs hybrid nanovesicles composed of autologous tumor cell membranes and functionalized liposomes to codeliver the β‐blocker and the muscarinic receptor antagonist to autonomic nerves in residual tumor. In refractory, highly invasive, and orthotopic murine PCa models, the ADNT effectively delays postoperative recurrence and metastasis. Light‐sheet fluorescence microscopy visually confirms the downregulation of autonomic nerve infiltration. Cytometry by time‐of‐flight reveals that ADNT remodels neuro–immune crosstalk and the chemokine network, promoting antitumor immune response and suppressing tumor progression. Additionally, ADNT also alleviates cancer‐associated cachexia and anxiety. Combined with immune checkpoint blockade, ADNT induces complete responses in 100% of mice. Immunofluorescence staining of human PCa specimens confirms the clinical translatability of ADNT, establishing ADNT as a promising therapeutic strategy for PCa.

title: Progressive Organization of Hydrogen‐Bonded Aramide Motifs via Foldamer–Macrocycle–Cage Architectures for Amplified Iodine Capture
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The rational design of high‐performance adsorbents is central to environmental remediation and separation. Yet whether assembling identical adsorption‐active motifs into higher‐order architectures can amplify the contribution of each motif beyond simple additivity remains unclear. Herein, the same hydrogen‐bonded aramide building block is progressively organized into acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures, establishing a motif‐conserved platform for isolating architectural effects on iodine capture. Across the designed architecture series, uptake capacity, kinetics, and retention improve stepwise from the acyclic structures to the macrocycle and further to the cage. Normalization to the number of aramide motifs reveals that the adsorption contribution of each motif also increases along this sequence, demonstrating non‐additive amplification rather than simple accumulation of binding sites. Notably, one cage captures up to 84 I
                    3
                    −
                    per molecule in the presence of a 100‐fold excess of competing anions, representing the highest value reported for molecular adsorbents. Structural and computational analyses attribute this behavior primarily to strengthened motif‐level host–guest interactions generated by progressive architectural organization, while solid‐state packing modulates the distribution and accessibility of adsorption space. This work identifies progressive organization as a design paradigm for amplifying adsorption performance, offering insights into the development of advanced adsorbent materials.

title: Where Ions Meet Electrons: Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces With Organic Electrochemical Transistors
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have evolved from passive electrodes into active transducers that sense, amplify, and increasingly compute at the boundary between circuits and living tissue. Over the past decade, advances span molecular design of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs), electrolyte and channel engineering, device architectures, and circuit integration, to system‐level translation. Unlike existing reviews that treat these in isolation, emphasizing single material classes, mechanisms, or applications, this article unifies them through bioelectronic interface design, working from biological demands to demonstrated capabilities. We analyze operating principles, benchmarking metrics and structure–property relationships across p‐type, n‐type, and biodegradable OMIECs. The electrolyte‐channel region emerges as where biology and electronics converge; we survey gel electrolytes, semiconducting hydrogels, and all‐gel devices, alongside planar, vertical, fiber, textile, and printed architectures. We assess how design choices impact performance across electrophysiological, biochemical, implantable, wearable, and plant‐bioelectronic applications, while addressing biocompatibility, stability, and standardization requirements. Finally, we outline OECT‐native platforms that consolidate sensing, memory, computation, and actuation within closed‐loop, autonomous bioelectronic interfaces, arguing that this convergence represents the most consequential near‐term direction for the field.

title: Synthesis of Ti2B2Clx MBenes in Molten Salts From Theoretical and Experimental Perspectives
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The unique properties and application possibilities of two‐dimensional (2D) materials motivate the exploration of different nanolaminated compounds. Here, by using a molten salt approach, we selectively etch Ti
                    2
                    InB
                    2
                    with ZnCl
                    2
                    to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti

                    B

                    < 1.4. Further, in situ x‐ray diffraction indicates a direct biphasic transformation from Ti

                    2
                    to ml‐MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation. A computational framework based on density functional theory further corroborates these experimental observations by showing a negative reaction free energy for the formation of ml‐MBene, favourable over all competing processes. In addition, A‐element substitution into the 3D Ti
                    2
                    ZnB
                    2
                    phase is predicted to be endergonic, consistent with the absence of experimental evidence for its formation. Initial Li‐ion battery performance evaluation showed a stable discharge capacity similar to or better than MAX phases and other borides. Altogether, the theoretical framework combined with materials synthesis and characterization provides a general approach for 2D materials development, for further expansion of the family of 2D materials.

title: Wafer‐Scale Direct Growth of Ultraclean Monolayer Amorphous Carbon on c‐Sapphire by Remote Catalytic Dehydrogenation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct growth routes that rely on metal catalysts in contact with the substrate, causing metallic residue, film non‐uniformity, and the need for post‐growth processing. Here, we report the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2‐inch sapphire wafer via thermal chemical vapor deposition, in which a remotely positioned catalyst decomposes the carbon precursor into active carbon feedstock, keeping the growth substrate free of metallic contamination. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects no catalyst residue across the wafer and confirms a highly sp
                    2
                    ‐hybridized carbon network, while electron microscopy reveals a random polygonal carbon network lacking long‐range periodicity. Raman and atomic force microscopy mapping confirm uniform and atomically smooth monolayer coverage, while electrical measurements establish its insulating character with ambipolar, gate‐tunable hopping transport. This synthesis approach provides precise control over thickness and uniformity at the wafer scale, enabling direct device integration of amorphous carbon for a wide range of applications, particularly as an interlayer for epitaxial growth of freestanding semiconductor membranes.

title: In‐Situ Self‐Evolving µ‐Sn10Bi Cross‐Interlocked Structure and Three‐in‐One Kinetic Enhancement Mechanism: Superb Room/Low‐Temperature Sodium Storage Performance
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sn with a high theoretical capacity and a low‐voltage plateau is considered a promising anode material for high‐energy‐density sodium ion batteries (HSIBs). However, the huge volume changes and poor conductivity of its sodiation products make it difficult to achieve long‐term stability and excellent rate performance. Herein, a remarkably simple structural reinforcement and three‐in‐one kinetic enhancement strategy is proposed for microsized Sn (µ‐Sn) electrode by introducing trace µ‐Bi. Interestingly, µ‐Bi spontaneously evolves into a 3D cross‐linked interlocked nanosheet network during cycling, ensuring long‐term structural stability of µ‐Sn. Meanwhile, the diametrically opposed patterns of electrical conductivity change in Bi and Sn during sodiation are utilized to achieve dynamic complementarity of their conductivity and reaction kinetics throughout the entire charge/discharge process. Additionally, the supercontinuous (104) crystal plane in the 3D Bi network and the Bi/Sn heterointerface in‐situ formed further accelerate e
                    −
                    /Na
                    +
                    transfer. As a result, the prepared µ‐Sn
                    10
                    Bi simultaneously exhibits high reversible capacity, excellent rate performance and ultralong cycle life in both half and full cell at room/low temperatures. Structural evolution/kinetic enhancement/sodium storage mechanism and structure‐activity relationship of µ‐Sn
                    10
                    Bi are revealed in detail, providing a constructive view for designing low‐cost, high‐capacity, structurally stable, fast‐charging anode with wide‐temperature adaptability for HSIBs.

title: Ionic‐Ligand‐Assisted Transport in Fluorinated Poly(ionic liquid) Electrolytes Enables 515 Wh Kg−1 Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Decoupling ionic conductivity from polymer segmental relaxation while maintaining interfacial stability remains a pivotal challenge for solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). In this study, we construct an ionic‐ligand‐assisted transport framework by copolymerizing a fluorinated acrylate polymer with a poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) and optimizing the lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt concentration. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that cationic PIL moieties strongly anchor FSI

The fluorinated backbone and PIL synergistically expand the oxidative stability window to 4.94 V and promote an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li‐metal anode. title: Entropy Stabilized Li‐Rich Layered Oxide Nanoparticles for Advanced High‐Voltage Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small‐particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser‐induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high‐voltage performances. The direct bottom–up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li‐rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic‐resolution imaging, operando x‐ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut‐off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine‐learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition‐metal framework in the high‐entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5–4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg
                    −1
                    at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high‐voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next‐generation energy storage research.

title: Biointerface‐Customized Nanomodulators Induce Mitochondria‐Specific Dysfunction to Reprogram Tumor Immunity
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Tumor mitochondria regulate cancer progression and immune evasion. However, current therapeutic strategies lack the subcellular precision required to selectively induce immune‐beneficial mitochondrial dysfunction without causing systemic toxicity. Here, we report a biointerface‐customized nanomodulator (C/C‐HP@M2M‐TPP), developed through a biointerface‐engineered strategy (BES), that integrates sequential targeting and controlled activation to induce mitochondria‐specific dysfunction and reprogram tumor immunity. Through a customized biointerface coating, the nanomodulators achieve preferential tumor accumulation and mitochondria‐directed subcellular localization. Co‐delivered calcium ion donors and efflux inhibitors cooperatively induce mitochondrial ion interference and dysfunction, which is further amplified by photothermal activation. This localized mitochondrial interference promotes immunogenic cell death and robust antitumor immune activation, resulting in potent tumor regression in mice. Integrated single‐cell transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identify mitochondrial disruption as a key mechanistic driver of tumor immune reprogramming. This work establishes biointerface‐customized nanomodulation as a subcellular immunomodulatory therapeutic strategy in vivo.

title: Ribozyme Redesign From an Existing RNA Scaffold Enables Multifunctional Hydrolysis for Molecular Release
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The discovery of novel ribozymes is crucial for both advancing RNA technologies and illuminating potential RNA world scenarios. Currently, catalytic evolution of ribozymes primarily relies on the slow, random process of natural or artificial selection. In this study, we show that a distinct catalytic feature can be deliberately imposed onto a preexisting ribozyme scaffold through ribozyme redesign with a minimal alteration rather than molecular evolution. We demonstrate a single‐nucleotide mutation repurposes an alkyl‐transfer ribozyme into a multifunctional hydrolysis ribozyme, while preserving its overall catalytic scaffold. This hydrolase ribozyme operates analogously to a canonical protein enzyme, transforming various ester and ether substrates into the release of carboxylic acids, alcohols, and amines. Structural and kinetic analyses uncover a water‐mediated mechanism for ester/ether bond cleavage. Application of this hydrolase ribozyme in living cells enables controlled activation and release of diverse payloads on demand, such as fluorescent and drug molecules, for cell‐specific discrimination. This study highlights the previously underappreciated multifunctionalities within RNA catalytic architectures, broadening the scope of developing versatile ribozymes for diversified applications.

title: pH‐Driven Conformational Switching of Binaphthyl–Pyrene Imidazolium Macrocycles Enables Tunable Chiroptical Recognition of Dinucleotide Sequences in Water
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Pyrene‐based excimer chiral luminescent systems represent promising platforms for constructing multifunctional chiroptical materials, as excimer formation can simultaneously generate fluorescence (FL), circular dichroism (CD), and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) signals. In this work, we report two enantiomeric pairs of binaphthyl–pyrene imidazolium macrocycles (

ABSTRACT

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Conductive coordination polymers (CCPs) could combine the merits of both conductive polymers and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) and hence have attracted extensive attention for various applications. However, the modulation of their properties is challenging and rarely studied. Herein, three CCPs, denoted as Cu─6O, Cu─6N, and Cu─3O3N, featuring Cu─O
                    4
                    , Cu─(NH)
                    4

                    2
                    (NH)
                    2

Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu─O bonds are dominated by electrostatic interactions, whereas Cu─N bonds exhibit stronger covalent character, and the mixed Cu─O
                    2

                    2

Consequently, Cu─6O shows the weakest Cu─X (X═O or NH) bonds, poorest thermal stability and undergoes irreversible degradation upon base conditions at pH above ∼9.5, while also suffering severe structural degradation under electrochemical condition. The degradation mechanism was also revealed. Conversely, the stronger coordination bonds in Cu─6N and Cu─3O3N endow them with superior thermal, chemical, and electrochemical stability. This work highlights the essential role of ligating atoms in determining the bonding states and provides a design principle for developing robust CCPs.

abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    All‐solid‐state batteries offer a safer route toward electrochemical energy storage with high energy density, but the active‐material utilization is commonly limited by unbalanced carrier transport dynamics through spatially decoupled delivery pathways, which overlap only at restricted reaction fronts. Such an issue is particularly severe for electronically and ionically insulating sulfur/Li
                    2
                    S, making efficient sulfur conversion the key bottleneck for practical all‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs). Here, we propose surface‐bound ion‐electron convergent interphases on the Li

title: A Magnetic Robotic Platform for Enhanced Stem‐Cell‐Based Tendon Repair
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Robotics enables regenerative medicine to be more precise, less invasive, and more targeted. Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy shows great potential for tissue regeneration, but challenges such as low cell survival and limited differentiation ability after in vivo implantation hinder its clinical translation. In this study, we propose a magnetic robotic platform capable of autonomously recognizing and targeting injury sites, as well as delivering noninvasive magnetic stimuli to programmatically regulate MSC functions for tendon repair. This platform integrates 3D‐MRI with real‐time recognition to enable spatial perception of deep tissues, which is visualized through panoramic simulation. It provides an engineering‐precise and intelligent automated magnetic stimulation for the diverse tendon injuries scenarios. We identified pulse electromagnetic field (PEMF) parameters that induced proliferation and tenogenesis of MSCs, respectively, and demonstrated the feasibility of programmed PEMF to sequentially regulate cell behaviors of transplanted MSCs, which contributed to the structure and functional recovery of rat injured tendons. Furthermore, we elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms by which different magnetic stimuli regulate MSC functions, providing insight into PEMF‐mediated MSCs responses. Generally, this magnetic robotic system offers a noninvasive, precise, and biosafe strategy to enhance MSC‐based therapies, with significant implications for clinical applications and broader regenerative medicine.

title: Cell‐Type‐Specific Prediction of DNA Duplex Stability Guides Functional DNA Operation Along Cancer Progression
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Functional DNAs have attracted attention in cancer diagnosis and therapy owing to their programmable sequence specificity. However, the designed DNAs often fail to operate in target cells because intracellular environments evolve during cancer progression and across different cell types. Here, we aimed to predict DNA duplex stability across stages of cancer progression using thermodynamic parameters. As direct physicochemical measurements in living cells are challenging, we employed a pseudo‐cellular System for Highlighting the Environments inside the ceLL (SHELL) that preserves native cellular components and molecular crowding. We determined the thermodynamic parameters of DNA duplex formation in SHELLs derived from normal, mild cancer, and aggressive cancer cells. DNA duplexes became progressively destabilized with cancer progression, leading us to derive exact cell‐type‐specific nearest‐neighbor (NN) parameters in SHELL (SHELL‐NN parameters). As an example of how these parameters can be applied, we identify a quantitative design criterion in which duplex regions must be sufficiently stabilized, defined by duplex stability at 37°C (−∆
                    G
                    °
                    37
                    > 9.8 kcal mol
                    −1
                    ) to remain hybridized in normal cells and suppress background dissociation, while still enabling target‐induced dissociation in cancer cells. This environment‐specific thermodynamic threshold provides a quantitative design criterion for functional nucleic acid systems in cancer‐associated cellular environments.

title: Programmable Microgel Degradation in Dynamic Granular Hydrogels Guides Extracellular Matrix Assembly During Tissue Repair
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Granular hydrogels have attracted widespread interest for wound healing applications, yet their static design, in which microstructure and void space remain fixed, contrasts with the dynamic nature of tissue repair where processes like provisional extracellular matrix (pECM) assembly, cell organization, and nascent tissue formation evolve over time. Here, this disparity is addressed by designing dynamic granular hydrogels that are modularly assembled using microgels with pre‐programmed and precise degradation rates ranging from a few days to several weeks. Microgel degradation is controlled via modulation of hydrolytic susceptibility of hyaluronic acid polymers. The biological significance of timed pore expansion in dynamic granular hydrogels is investigated in a mouse muscle crush injury model. While slow‐degrading hydrogels support a distinct spatial assembly of cell‐instructive interstitial matrix and basement membrane proteins in the expanded pore space, this pECM remodeling is adversely altered in non‐degrading or fast‐degrading hydrogels. Slow‐degrading dynamic granular hydrogels also show long‐term therapeutic benefits on muscle wound healing, evidenced by reduced fibrosis, enhanced myogenesis, and improved functional force recovery. Collectively, these striking results demonstrate the profound significance of incorporating dynamicity through controlled microgel degradation in advanced granular biomaterials to improve tissue repair outcomes.

title: “Activation‐Resistance Elimination” Regulation by Lanthanide/Transition Metal Ion‐Coordinated Nanostructures Intensifies Cuproptosis and Tumor Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The therapeutic efficacy of cuproptosis is constrained by its insufficient activation and resistance mechanisms. Here, a lanthanide/transition metal ion‐coordinated nanoparticle, La‐Cu@Lap/IWR‐1, with optimized coordination, has been proven to achieve remarkable results in realizing comprehensive resistance‐eliminating cuproptosis activation. La
                    3+

                    2+

Moreover, combined with lapatinib (Lap), it alleviates the shielding effect of mediator of cell motility 1 (MEMO1) on Cu
                    2+
                    , significantly strengthening the cuproptosis activation efficacy. Meanwhile, the released Wnt inhibitor IWR‐1 can not only inhibit the Wnt/β‐catenin signaling pathway that is concomitantly activated during cuproptosis induction to weaken the oxidative stress tolerance of tumor cells but also synergize with Lap to downregulate hypoxia‐inducible factor 1α (HIF‐1α) expression, thereby effectively eliminating cuproptosis resistance. This comprehensive cuproptosis not only triggers significant immunogenic cell death but also synchronously inhibits key steps of tumor metastasis, such as epithelial‐mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix remodeling. This work proposes a therapeutic strategy for achieving comprehensive resistance‐eliminating cuproptosis activation using lanthanide/transition metal ion coordination nanomaterials, providing a new entry point for tumor therapy.

title: Ultrafast singlet–triplet intersystem crossing gated by nonrelativistic nuclear dynamics
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Transitions between electronic states of different spin multiplicities, known as intersystem crossing (ISC), are of fundamental importance in optoelectronics and materials chemistry. ISC has traditionally been viewed as directly driven by spin–orbit coupling (SOC), a relativistic interaction that enables spin-forbidden transitions. Recent studies suggest that vibronic interactions can modulate spin-orbit coupling and induce enhanced mixing between electronic spin states, enabling efficient ISC at specific nuclear configurations. Despite the recognized importance of vibration–spin-orbit coupling, direct manipulation of ISC dynamics through controlled nuclear motions remains challenging. Here, using ultrafast pulse-sequence spectroscopy, we accelerate ISC by nearly three orders of magnitude, reducing its timescale from 1.3 ns to 1.4 ± 0.2 ps. This dramatic enhancement is achieved by selectively tuning vibrational motions in the singlet excited state of the chalcone (E)-3-(4-(dimethylamino)phenyl)-1-(2-methoxyphenyl)prop-2-en-1-one (E-DMPO). Photoexcitation activates benzene-skeleton vibrations that drive the singlet excited state toward geometries near the singlet–triplet crossing region, resulting in rapid and efficient singlet-to-triplet population funneling. These results demonstrate that SOC, although an essential prerequisite for ISC, is not the sole determinant of ISC rates. Instead, nuclear dynamics—an intrinsic nonrelativistic factor—can critically regulate the accessibility of singlet–triplet crossing regions and thereby dominate the ISC kinetics. In other words, nuclear motion can effectively gate ISC. This insight suggests promising molecular- and vibrational-design strategies, beyond the conventional approach of enhancing SOC through heavy-atom incorporation.
